metadata.author: Anil
metadata.summary: A traveler boards the last train of the night and finds a sealed envelope addressed to him in handwriting he recognizes from ten years ago — a dead man's hand.
metadata.hook: The envelope was sealed. The sender had been dead for a decade.

characters.name: Arun
characters.motivation: Running away from a past he never reconciled
characters.wound: Lost his closest friend under circumstances he blames himself for
characters.flaw: Avoids confrontation; destroys evidence of pain rather than processing it

characters.name: Deepak
characters.motivation: Left something unfinished; the letter is his last act
characters.arc: Revealed slowly through the letter's contents

paragraphs.text: Arun boarded the last train just as the station clock struck eleven. The platform was nearly empty, and a pale mist drifted between the iron pillars like something that had forgotten how to leave.

He chose a window seat in a carriage that smelled faintly of rain and old paper. On the seat beside him lay an envelope. His name was written on the front in blue ink — a hand he had not seen in ten years, and had never expected to see again.
Deepak had been buried in the winter of 1988. Arun himself had stood at the graveside, collar up against the cold, telling himself it was not his fault. He had almost believed it by now.
When he opened the letter, the train lurched forward, and the city lights began to fall away into darkness. The first line read: *I know what you told them. I know what you left out.*
